subject: math
title: Vector Algebra
syllabus: Vectors and scalars, the addition of vectors, components of a vector in two dimensions and three-dimensional space, scalar and vector products.

body: a⃗·b⃗ = a_{1}b_{1} + a_{2}b_{2} + a_{3}b_{3} = |a⃗||b⃗| cos θ. Zero ⇔ perpendicular; negative ⇔ obtuse angle.
Projection (length) of a⃗ on b⃗: \f{a⃗·b⃗}{|b⃗|}. Projection vector: \f{a⃗·b⃗}{|b⃗|^{2}}b⃗.
a⃗ = (part along b⃗) + (part ⟂ b⃗); the perpendicular part is a⃗ − \f{a⃗·b⃗}{|b⃗|^{2}}b⃗.
The bisector of the angle between a⃗ and b⃗ is along â + b̂.

check.why: Dot with the unit vector î.

body: a⃗ × b⃗ is ⟂ to both, with |a⃗ × b⃗| = |a⃗||b⃗| sin θ = area of the parallelogram on a⃗, b⃗.
Triangle area \f{1}{2}|AB⃗ × AC⃗|; parallelogram from diagonals: \f{1}{2}|d⃗_{1} × d⃗_{2}|.
[a⃗ b⃗ c⃗] = a⃗·(b⃗ × c⃗) = the 3 × 3 determinant; |…| = volume of the parallelepiped; zero ⇔ coplanar.
Solving: (pa⃗ + qb⃗) × c⃗ = 0 ⇒ c⃗ = t(pa⃗ + qb⃗); a⃗ × c⃗ = b⃗ ⇒ c⃗ = c⃗_{0} + ta⃗. A dot condition then fixes t.

traps: Projection divides by |b⃗|, the projection VECTOR by |b⃗|^{2}.
a⃗ × b⃗ ≠ b⃗ × a⃗ — order flips the sign.
Area of a triangle needs the ½.
From a⃗ × c⃗ = a⃗ × b⃗ you only get c⃗ − b⃗ ∥ a⃗, not c⃗ = b⃗.
Check a⃗·b⃗ = 0 before solving a⃗ × c⃗ = b⃗ — otherwise there is no solution.
Diagonals give area ½|d⃗_{1} × d⃗_{2}|, not |d⃗_{1} × d⃗_{2}|.

pyq.q: If a⃗ is a nonzero vector such that its projections on the vectors 2î − ĵ + 2k̂, î + 2ĵ − 2k̂ and k̂ are equal, then a unit vector along a⃗ is :
sol: Both vectors have length 3. With a⃗ = (x, y, z): \f{2x − y + 2z}{3} = \f{x + 2y − 2z}{3} = z.

pyq.q: The set of all α, for which the vector a⃗ = αtî + 6ĵ − 3k̂ and b⃗ = tî − 2ĵ − 2αtk̂ are inclined at an obtuse angle for all t ∈ ℝ is :
sol: Need a⃗·b⃗ = αt^{2} + 6αt − 12 < 0 for every t.
α = 0 gives −12 < 0 ✓. For α ≠ 0 need α < 0 and discriminant 36α^{2} + 48α < 0 → −\f{4}{3} < α < 0.

Between the following two statements : Statement-I : Let a⃗ = î + 2ĵ − 3k̂ and b⃗ = 2î + ĵ − k̂. Then the vector r⃗ satisfying a⃗ × r⃗ = a⃗ × b⃗ and a⃗·r⃗ = 0 is of magnitude √{10}. Statement-II : In a triangle ABC, cos 2A + cos 2B + cos 2C ≥ −\f{3}{2}.
sol: II: cos 2A + cos 2B + cos 2C = −1 − 4 cos A cos B cos C ≥ −\f{3}{2}, since cos A cos B cos C ≤ \f{1}{8}: true.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect

sol: Circle: no xy term → K^{2} − 5K + 4 = 0 → K = 1, 4; equal x^{2}, y^{2} coefficients → K^{2} = 3K − 2 → K = 1, 2.

Let a⃗_{k} = (tan θ_{k})î + ĵ and b⃗_{k} = î − (cot θ_{k})ĵ, where θ_{k} = \f{2^{k−1}π}{2^{n} + 1}, for some n ∈ ℕ, n > 5. Then the value of \f{Σ_{k=1}^{n}|a⃗_{k}|^{2}}{Σ_{k=1}^{n}|b⃗_{k}|^{2}} is ______.

The ratio comes out 3 for every n (checked numerically for n = 6 … 11).
